axes.title: Cyclic graph ownership and garbage collection

lastLight.scenario: The Last Light menu graph keeps parent links weak, children shared, and observer callbacks explicitly drained.
lastLight.expectedUse: Cycles with a known weak edge or service boundary compose. A transparent collector is not a baseline memory mechanism.

axes.sameProblem: Represent a graph with back edges and reclaim resources without leaks, use-after-free, or hidden shutdown order.
axes.globalSimplification: Use one owner, weak-edge, and close model. Do not add a second collector lifecycle for graph-shaped data.

c.problem: Represent and reclaim a graph with back edges.
c.mechanism: Raw pointers and manual destruction represent edges; cycle collection is a library or application policy.
c.operationalTradeoff: The owner graph and release order are not inferred by the language.

rust.problem: Represent and reclaim a graph with back edges.
rust.mechanism: Rc and Weak provide reference-counted graph edges with explicit weak back references.
rust.operationalTradeoff: A strong cycle remains until an edge is weakened or a separate cycle policy breaks it.

python.problem: Represent and reclaim a graph with back edges.
python.mechanism: Reference counting is supplemented by an optional cyclic garbage collector with debugging and uncollectable states.
python.operationalTradeoff: Collection timing and finalization are runtime policy, not a source ownership edge.

wCurrentComposition.attempt: Compose shared and weak handles, lexical cleanup, service drain, callback leases, and explicit graph identity.

intentionalTradeoff.reason: Resource cleanup order and external effects stay observable.

axes.title: Shared-memory IPC and memory mapping

lastLight.scenario: The Last Light telemetry path snapshots files, archives Parquet, hands typed rows through Arrow IPC, and imports a trusted C Data carrier.
lastLight.expectedUse: Portable snapshots and typed IPC compose today. A process-shared mapped region needs explicit layout, atomics, crash, and capability contracts.

axes.sameProblem: Share the same backing bytes between processes through a mapped region without invalid pointers, torn values, stale mappings, or undeclared authority.
axes.globalSimplification: Use one explicit boundary family: snapshot or typed wire first, mapped bytes only after layout, atomic, crash, and capability facts are proven.

c.problem: Share data through a process-shared mapped region.
c.mechanism: POSIX shm_open and mmap establish a named object and map bytes into a process address space.
c.provenance: POSIX platform API; this is not a C-language capability.
c.operationalTradeoff: The bytes, layout, synchronization, lifetime, and crash behavior remain application contracts.

rust.problem: Share data through a process-shared mapped region.
rust.mechanism: Rust safe ownership covers process-local values; mapping and process-shared layout require an OS or FFI contract outside std ownership.
rust.operationalTradeoff: A mapped pointer is not a valid Rust reference in another address space without a typed representation and synchronization proof.

python.problem: Share data through a process-shared mapped region.
python.mechanism: multiprocessing.shared_memory attaches named volatile blocks and exposes close/unlink lifecycle operations.
python.operationalTradeoff: The block is bytes with restricted values; process cleanup, tracker behavior, and synchronization remain runtime/provider concerns.

wCurrentComposition.attempt: Compose root-scoped filesystem, bounded snapshots, wWire/Arrow carriers, C Data adapters, atomics, and explicit service channels.

exactGap.notProposed: A raw mapped pointer or transparent shared-memory type with hidden process identity.
